transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Cora Vakulman.
President Trump travels to Alaska today
to continue campaigning for Republican candidates
ahead of the November midterm elections.
They're three weeks from today.
NPR's Danielle Kurtzleben reports
the president was in Ohio last night
speaking at a GOP rally in Youngstown.
President Trump told the Ohio crowd
a message he's given at several rallies this year.
Just pretend that I'm on the ballot.
Because in a way I am on the ballot
'cause they will try and destroy everything we've done.
Trump is not on the midterm ballot,
but he has been stumping in states
he won by double digit margins in 2024 like Ohio and Texas.
Today he heads to Alaska
and he will visit deep red Montana later in the week.
He also has planned events in Georgia and Arizona.
Trump has said he thinks these rallies boost turnout.
There are tight midterm races even in some red states
and the president's approval is below 40% in many polls.
Danielle Kurtzleben, NPR News.
Intelligence sharing between two allies,
the U.S. and South Korea, has run into difficulty.
NPR's Anthony Kuhn reports
that's according to Seoul's envoy to Washington.
The Yonhap News Agency reports
that South Korea's ambassador to the U.S.,
Kang Kyung-hwa told lawmakers that as she put it,
quote, "There are limitations in our communication
with the White House," unquote,
and that she was frustrated by infrequent high-level access.
South Korean media reported
that the U.S. excluded South Korea's spy agency
from trilateral talks with Japan in June.
The reports link this to the South's unification minister's
public mention of a North Korean uranium enrichment facility.
The minister argues that the facility
was already a matter of public knowledge.
South Korea's spy agency denies
that any less intelligence is being shared,
including regarding North Korea's missile tests,
of which there have been four over the last month.
Anthony Kuhn, NPR News, Seoul.
More than 60,000 Florida customers are still in the dark
after Hurricane Isaias made landfall
on the coast of the Gulf last Friday.
The storm killed four people.
Stocks opened mixed this morning
as home sales show a modest pickup.
NPR's Scott Horsley reports
that Dow Jones' industrial average
lost about five points in early trading.
The National Association of Realtors says
sales of existing homes rose by 1.5% last month
after a lackluster summer.
September sales were still down from a year ago.
High mortgage rates have been a drag on home sales,
but that hasn't put much of a dent in home prices.
The average sales price last month topped $417,000.
Some of the nation's biggest banks
are reporting earnings today.
JPMorgan Chase says quarterly profits
were up 6% from a year ago,
but forecasters were expecting even stronger results.
And the International Monetary Fund has raised its forecast
for global economic growth this year to 3.1%,
despite the headwinds of high energy prices
caused by the U.S. war with Iran.
Scott Horsley, NPR News, Washington.
You're listening to NPR.
The White House says that the U.S. Ambassador to Greece,
Kimberly Guilfoyle, has been asked to resign.
That is, after reports surfaced in the Wall Street Journal
alleging she had engaged in potentially illegal conduct.
That includes an allegation
that she used her diplomatic position
to obtain money from donors.
Guilfoyle has denied any wrongdoing.
Guilfoyle was once engaged to be married to Donald Trump Jr.
Nearly 14 million homes
will hit the market over the next decade
as boomers and other older owners sell.
But NPR's Jennifer Ledin reports
that Wave will not offer much help to first-time buyers.
Coming years will see a 30% jump in housing inventory.
According to a new analysis by Realtor.com,
most homes freed up will be larger, family-sized,
and that could soften the market at a time
when many people are priced out.
But only a few hundred thousand will be smaller,
so-called starter homes.
In part, the report says that's because those owners
are more likely to have paid off their mortgage
and stay put longer.
This generational transfer will also play out slowly.
Housing analysts say the so-called silver tsunami
is not likely to close the current housing shortage.
The oldest baby boomers turn 80 this year,
a turning point when homeownership starts to decline.
Jennifer Ledin, NPR News, Washington.
Pope Leo has arrived at a Rome hospital for surgery.
He announced over the weekend
he's having a small localized nodule
removed from one of his lungs.
The Vatican says it expects him to take a week to recover.
This is NPR.
Simple. This message comes from Kachava.
Sometimes, flavors need a pinch of salt
to unleash their full potential, kind of like life.
A little saltiness can keep things interesting
and deliciously sweet.
Fuel your salty sweet cravings
with Kachava's new salted caramel all-in-one nutrition shake.
Just two scoops provide protein, fiber, greens, and more.
Embrace your salty side.
Go to kachava.com and use code NPR
for 15% off your first order.
That's K-A-C-H-A-V-A dot com code NPR.

topics.text: Trump campaigns for GOP midterm candidates in Ohio, heads to Alaska, Montana, Georgia, Arizona
U.S.-South Korea intelligence sharing hits difficulty, per Seoul's ambassador Kang Kyung-hwa
Hurricane Isaias landfall on Gulf coast leaves 60,000 Florida customers without power, four dead
Stocks mixed as existing home sales rise 1.5% last month; JPMorgan Chase reports 6% profit gain
IMF raises 2026 global growth forecast to 3.1% despite high energy prices from U.S. war with Iran
White House asks U.S. Ambassador to Greece Kimberly Guilfoyle to resign after Wall Street Journal reports
Nearly 14 million boomer-owned homes expected to hit market over next decade, few starter homes
Pope Leo undergoes surgery at Rome hospital to remove lung nodule, expected week-long recovery
